--- title: "SPR Cup Analysis" bibliography: references.bib editor: markdown: wrap: 72 --- # Set Up ## Overview This analysis was originally developed for the 21st Annual Sloboda and Bukoski SPR Cup, presented at the Society for Prevention Research 34th Annual Meeting [@marcus2026]. It tests a residual-based model of resilience using the Add Health dataset ([@harris2013], specifically Waves I and III (*N* = 4,882) and can be broken down into the following steps: [Step 0: Disadvantage Composites]: indicators are used to build **outcome-specific disadvantage composites** [@marquez2023] [Step 1: Cumulative Disadvantage to Outcome]: **regress** each outcome on those composites [@miller-lewis2013] [Step 2: Residuals]: Extract residuals from those regressions to create **continuous** **resilience scores** (better- or worse-than-expected adaptation given disadvantage exposure). [Step 3: Protective Factors]: Multilevel resilience factors (individual, family, school, community) are tested as **predictors of resilience**, first in the full sample. [Step 4: Protective vs. Promotive]: Create high-disadvantage subsamples to distinguish between **promotive effects** (help regardless of disadvantage level) and **protective effects** (buffer specifically under high disadvantage). **Load Packages** All analyses use survey-weighted regression (`survey`) to account for Add Health's complex sampling design, with `gtsummary`/`flextable`/`gt` for APA-style output tables. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(gtsummary) # regression summary tables library(flextable) # table formatting and export library(gtools) # quantile splitting library(haven) # read SPSS .sav files library(tidyverse) # data wrangling library(survey) # complex survey / weighted regression library(broom) # tidy model output library(gt) # formatted tables ``` ::: The analytic dataset is the merged Add Health restricted-use survey data (`AddHealth_AllData.sav`), read in with `haven::read_sav()`. Import code is included but not rendered below. ## Data Cleaning (SPSS) Variable recoding, dummy coding, and composite construction for this project were done in SPSS prior to import into R, across four syntax files by domain (demographics, structural disadvantage, outcomes, protective factors). Each is excerpted below to document the approach. ### Demographics `Demographics.sps` recodes core demographic variables (child sex, age, race/ethnicity) into analysis-ready measures, checking frequencies before and after each recode. ``` spss *****************************CHILD SEX. *Q: What is your biological sex? ***check frequencies for zeros. frequencies variables = bio_sex /statistics = all. *male = 1, female = 2. *create dummy code for child biological sex (female = 1). if(bio_sex eq 1) bio_sexD = 0. if(bio_sex eq 2) bio_sexD = 1. variable labels bio_sexD "child biological sex". value labels bio_sexD 0 "male" 1 "female". execute. *check frequencies of new variable. frequencies variables = bio_sexD /statistics = all. ``` ### Structural Disadvantage `Disadvantage.sps` (672 lines) builds individual- and household-level disadvantage indicators, including race/ethnicity dummy codes with missing-data recodes. ``` spss *****************************FAMILY SOCIOECONOMIC DISADVANTAGE COMPOSITE. *Components: famincomecat (continuous $, higher = more income), pareduc_avg (0-8, higher = more education), parentemploy (0-1, higher = more employment). **Standardizing each component to z-score then reverse code so higher is more disadvantage, then take the average of all variables. *standardize based on weight filtered dataset. delete variables Zfamincomecat Zpareduc_avg Zparentemploy. *delete variable if previously standardized with whole sample. temporary. *temporary can't be used with delete. select if (GSWGT3_2 ge 0). descriptives variables = famincomecat pareduc_avg parentemploy /save. *Creates Zfamincomecat, Zpareduc_avg, Zparentemploy. execute. compute Zfamincomecat_r = Zfamincomecat * -1. variable labels Zfamincomecat_r "Family income z-scored reversed (higher = lower income = more disadvantage)". execute. compute Zpareduc_avg_r = Zpareduc_avg * -1. variable labels Zpareduc_avg_r "Average parental education z-scored reversed (higher = less education = more disadvantage)". execute. compute Zparentemploy_r = Zparentemploy * -1. variable labels Zparentemploy_r "Average parental employment z-scored reversed (higher = less employed = more disadvantage)". execute. compute famSES_disadv = mean(Zfamincomecat_r, Zpareduc_avg_r, Zparentemploy_r). variable labels famSES_disadv "Family SES disadvantage composite: mean of z-scored reversed income, education, employment (higher = more disadvantage)". execute. frequencies variables = famSES_disadv /statistics = all. reliability variables = famincomecat pareduc_avg parentemploy /scale('famSES') all /statistics = all. *standardize based on weight filtered dataset. temporary. select if (GSWGT3_2 ge 0). descriptives variables = famSES_disadv /save. *Creates Zfamincomecat, Zpareduc_avg, Zparentemploy. execute. ``` ### Outcomes `Outcomes.sps` (473 lines) constructs the substance-use outcome variable (alcohol, cigarette, and tobacco use composite), depression, general health, and educational attainment. Below is a exert from the final section of scoring the depression outcome. ``` spss *****************************CES-D DEPRESSION COMPOSITE (WAVE 3). *9 items (all in same 0-3 direction after reverse coding H3SP7 and H3SP11 above). *Sum score (0-27 range); Desch et al. (2023). compute cesD_sum = sum(dep_bothered, dep_blues, dep_asgood, dep_concentrate, dep_depressed, dep_tired, dep_enjoyed, dep_sad, dep_disliked). variable labels cesD_sum "CES-D depression sum score Wave 3 (0-27, higher = more depressive symptoms)". execute. reliability variables = dep_bothered dep_blues dep_asgood dep_concentrate dep_depressed dep_tired dep_enjoyed dep_sad dep_disliked /scale('CESD') all /statistics = all. frequencies variables = cesD_sum /statistics = all. *standardize based on weight filtered dataset. delete variables ZcesD_sum. *delete variable if previously standardized with whole sample. temporary. *temporary can't be used with delete. select if (GSWGT3_2 ge 0). descriptives variables = cesD_sum / save. ``` ### Protective Factors `Protective.sps` (887 lines) builds the protective-factor composites, several of which are reverse-scored so that higher values consistently indicate greater disadvantage.Below is an example of the data cleaning of one variable and then the creation of one protective factor composite. ``` spss ***************************COMMUNITY RESOURCES - CONNECTEDNESS (ADOLESCENT REPORT). *Note: Items reverse-scored here so higher = LOWER community resources (disadvantage direction), *consistent with the structural disadvantage framing of this composite. *Community Connectedness (Wickrama & Bryant 2003): 4 items, yes/no (0/1), summed 0-4. *Reverse scoring: recode 1->0 and 0->1 so high score = LOW connectedness = more disadvantage. if (H1NB1 eq 1) knowneighbR = 0. *knows neighbors = connected (reverse to 0=low disadvantage). if (H1NB1 eq 2) knowneighbR = 1. *doesn't know = disconnected = higher disadvantage. if (H1NB1 eq 6 or H1NB1 eq 8 or H1NB1 eq 9) knowneighbR = -99. recode knowneighbR (-99 = sysmis). variable labels knowneighbR "Does NOT know most neighbors (H1NB1 reversed, 1=low connectedness/more disadvantage)". value labels knowneighbR 0 "knows most neighbors" 1 "does not know most neighbors". execute. ***************************COMMUNITY CONNECTEDNESS INDEX (Wickrama & Bryant 2003). *Items coded in protective direction (1 = connected): *knowneighb, talkneighb, neighbwatch, nbhdsafe. *Sum 0-4; higher = more connectedness = more protective. compute commconnect = sum(knowneighb, talkneighb, neighbwatch, nbhdsafe). variable labels commconnect "Community connectedness (Wickrama & Bryant 2003, sum 0-4, higher = more connectedness)". execute. reliability variables = knowneighb talkneighb neighbwatch nbhdsafe /scale('commconnect') all /statistics = all. *alpha = .51. frequencies variables = commconnect /statistics = all. *standardize based on weight filtered dataset. delete variables Zcommconnect. *delete variable if previously standardized with whole sample. temporary. *temporary can't be used with delete. select if (GSWGT3_2 ge 0). descriptives variables = commconnect / save. ******************************************************************************* ``` The cleaned file was exported and merged into `AddHealth_AllData.sav` for the R analysis above. ## Survey Design Specification Add Health uses a complex, clustered, stratified sampling design. All regressions use the Wave 3 grand sample weight (`GSWGT3_2_2`) via the `survey` package to produce design-consistent estimates. **Missing Sample Weight at Wave 3** Respondents missing GSWGT3_2 were not part of the Wave 3 sample (e.g., lost to follow-up, deceased, ineligible) and should be excluded from analysis ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} #how many cases missing cat("Missing GSWGT3_2:", sum(is.na(dat$GSWGT3_2)), "\n") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Missing GSWGT3_2: 1622 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} cat("Non-missing GSWGT3_2:", sum(!is.na(dat$GSWGT3_2)), "\n") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Non-missing GSWGT3_2: 4882 ``` ::: ::: **Filtered Dataset** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # ── Subset to respondents with valid Wave 3 weight ──────────────────────────── dat_w3 <- dat |> filter(!is.na(GSWGT3_2)) #dat_w3 is name of filtered dataset cat("Analytic n after excluding missing weights:", nrow(dat_w3), "\n") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Analytic n after excluding missing weights: 4882 ``` ::: ::: **Sample Weighted Dataset** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # ── Specify survey design on the subsetted data ─────────────────────────────── # Use design_w3 as survey weight design in regressions # svydesign() with ids = ~1 specifies no clustering beyond the given weights # Add Health's Wave 3 grand sample weight (GSWGT3_2) adjusts for unequal selection probability and non-response so estimates generalize to the population design_w3 <- svydesign( ids = ~1, weights = ~GSWGT3_2, data = dat_w3) cat("Sum of weights:", round(sum(dat_w3$GSWGT3_2), 0), "\n") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Sum of weights: 22144327 ``` ::: ::: ## Descriptive Statistics Create @tbl-descriptives to display the *M*, *SD*, and range of each analytic variable. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # ── Variable lists with display labels ──────────────────────────────────────── disadvantage_vars <- c( "minorityD" = "Minority Status", "school_disadv" = "School Disadvantage", "econhardship" = "Economic Hardship", "famSES_disadv" = "Family SES Disadvantage", "nbhd_subj_disadv" = "Neighborhood Disadvantage (Subjective)", "cens_nbhd_disadv" = "Neighborhood Disadvantage (Census)") protective_vars <- c( "commconnect" = "Community Connectedness", "commintegr_disadv" = "Community Integration", "opt_hopeful" = "Optimism / Hopefulness", "selfesteem" = "Self-Esteem", "self_efficacy" = "Self-Efficacy", "parentchild_rel" = "Parent-Child Relationship", "schoolconnect" = "School Connectedness") outcome_vars <- c( "cesD_sum" = "Depression Symptoms", "subuse_W3" = "Substance Use", "edattain_W3" = "Education Attainment", "genhealth_W3"= "General Health") # ── Function: get weighted M and SD, and unweighted range ───────────────────── get_desc <- function(var, design) { mn <- as.numeric(svymean(as.formula(paste0("~", var)), design, na.rm = TRUE)) vr <- as.numeric(svyvar(as.formula(paste0("~", var)), design, na.rm = TRUE)) rng <- range(design$variables[[var]], na.rm = TRUE) data.frame( M = formatC(mn, digits = 2, format = "f"), SD = formatC(sqrt(vr), digits = 2, format = "f"), Range = paste0(formatC(rng[1], digits = 2, format = "f"), "–", formatC(rng[2], digits = 2, format = "f"))) } # ── Build rows for each variable group ──────────────────────────────────────── make_desc_rows <- function(var_named_vec, design, section_label) { rows <- lapply(names(var_named_vec), function(v) { d <- get_desc(v, design) data.frame(Variable = var_named_vec[[v]], M = d$M, SD = d$SD, Range = d$Range) }) rows <- do.call(rbind, rows) rbind(data.frame(Variable = section_label, M = "", SD = "", Range = ""), rows) } desc_tbl <- rbind( make_desc_rows(disadvantage_vars, design_w3, "Disadvantage Predictors"), make_desc_rows(protective_vars, design_w3, "Protective Factors"), make_desc_rows(outcome_vars, design_w3, "Outcomes")) # ── Build flextable ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── header_rows <- which(desc_tbl$M == "") header_rows <- which(desc_tbl$M == "") descriptives <- flextable(desc_tbl) |> set_header_labels(Variable = "Variable", M = "M", SD = "SD", Range = "Range") |> add_header_row( values = c("", "Weighted Descriptive Statistics"), colwidths = c(1, 3) # was c(1, 2) ) |> theme_apa() |> font(fontname = "Times New Roman", part = "all") |> fontsize(size = 11, part = "all") |> bold(part = "header") |> bold(i = header_rows, part = "body") |> width(j = 1, width = 3.0) |> width(j = 2:4, width = 1.0) |> # was 2:3 align(j = 2:4, align = "center", part = "all") |> # was 2:3 padding(i = setdiff(seq_len(nrow(desc_tbl)), header_rows), j = 1, padding.left = 20, part = "body") |> add_footer_lines("Note. Means and standard deviations are weighted using the Wave 3 grand sample weight (GSWGT3_2). Range is unweighted.") |> fontsize(size = 9, part = "footer") |> italic(part = "footer") ``` ::: ::: {#tbl-descriptives .cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: The analytic sample reports moderate average levels of structural disadvantage (e.g., *M* = 0.52 school disadvantage on a 0–3 scale) alongside relatively high protective-factor scores (e.g., *M* = 4.15 parent-child relationship on a 1–5 scale), consistent with a normative, not exclusively high-risk, longitudinal sample. # Step 0: Disadvantage Composites {#step0} ## Individual Disadvantage Regressions The next several chunks repeat the same regression for each structural disadvantage indicator (minority status, school, economic, family SES, neighborhood subjective/census) predicting each outcome (depression, substance use, educational attainment, general health). Each regression uses the standardized outcome and standardized predictor variable, and each chunk stores the beta and p-value, which become the weights used to build the cumulative disadvantage composite in the [Step 1: Cumulative Disadvantage to Outcome] section below. ::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon="false"} **Regress outcome on structural disadvantage indicator.** `outcome_disadvantage <-` `svyglm(outcome ~ disadvantage, design = design_w3, family = gaussian())` ::: ::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon="false"} **Extra standardized betas for later beta-weighted composites.** `dat_w3$outcome_disadvantage <- coef(outcome_disadvantage)[2]` ::: ::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon="false"} **Extra standardized betas and p values for predictor weight table.** `outcome_disadvantageB<- coef(outcome_disadvantage[2]` `outcome_disadvantageP` `<-summary(outcome_disadvantage)$coefficients["disadvantage","Pr(\>\|t\|)"\]` ::: ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal" icon="false"} Jump to @tbl-disadvantage-weight-table to see the results of the individual disadvantage regressions. ::: **Depression** Depression Weights - Minority Status ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # run regression depression_minorityD <- svyglm( ZcesD_sum ~ minorityD, design = design_w3, family = gaussian() ) #save beta and p value dat_w3$dep_minorityD <- coef(depression_minorityD)[2] dep_minorityD_B <- coef(depression_minorityD)[2] dep_minorityD_P <-summary(depression_minorityD)$coefficients["minorityD", "Pr(>|t|)"] ``` ::: Depression Weights - School Disadvantage ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # run regression depression_school_disadv <- svyglm( ZcesD_sum ~ Zschool_disadv, design = design_w3, family = gaussian() ) #save beta and p value dat_w3$dep_school <- coef(depression_school_disadv)[2] dep_school_B <- coef(depression_school_disadv)[2] dep_school_P <-summary(depression_school_disadv)$coefficients["Zschool_disadv", "Pr(>|t|)"] ``` ::: Depression Weights - Economic Hardship ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # run regression depression_econhardship <- svyglm( ZcesD_sum ~ Zeconhardship, design = design_w3, family = gaussian() ) #save beta and p value dat_w3$dep_econ <- coef(depression_econhardship)[2] dep_econ_B <- coef(depression_econhardship)[2] dep_econ_P <-summary(depression_econhardship)$coefficients["Zeconhardship", "Pr(>|t|)"] ``` ::: Depression Weights - Family SES ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # run regression depression_famSES_disadv <- svyglm( ZcesD_sum ~ famSES_disadv, design = design_w3, family = gaussian() ) #save beta and p value dat_w3$dep_fam <- coef(depression_famSES_disadv)[2] dep_famSES_B <- coef(depression_famSES_disadv)[2] dep_famSES_P <-summary(depression_famSES_disadv)$coefficients["famSES_disadv", "Pr(>|t|)"] ``` ::: Depression Weights - Neighborhood Disadvantage, Subjective ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # run regression depression_nbhd_subj_disadv <- svyglm( ZcesD_sum ~ Znbhd_subj_disadv, design = design_w3, family = gaussian() ) #save beta and p value dat_w3$dep_nbhdsub <- coef(depression_nbhd_subj_disadv)[2] dep_nbhdsub_B <- coef(depression_nbhd_subj_disadv)[2] dep_nbhdsub_P <-summary(depression_nbhd_subj_disadv)$coefficients["Znbhd_subj_disadv", "Pr(>|t|)"] ``` ::: Depression Weights - Neighborhood Disadvantage, Census ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # run regression depression_cens_nbhd_disadv <- svyglm( ZcesD_sum ~ Zcens_nbhd_disadv, design = design_w3, family = gaussian() ) #save beta and p value dat_w3$dep_censnbhd <- coef(depression_cens_nbhd_disadv)[2] dep_censnbhd_B <- coef(depression_cens_nbhd_disadv)[2] dep_censnbhd_P <-summary(depression_cens_nbhd_disadv)$coefficients["Zcens_nbhd_disadv", "Pr(>|t|)"] ``` ::: **Substance Use** Substance Use Weights - Minority Status ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # run regression substance_minorityD <- svyglm( Zsubuse_W3 ~ minorityD, design = design_w3, family = gaussian() ) #save beta and p value dat_w3$substance_minorityD <- coef(substance_minorityD)[2] substance_minorityD_B <- coef(substance_minorityD)[2] substance_minorityD_P <-summary(substance_minorityD)$coefficients["minorityD", "Pr(>|t|)"] ``` ::: Substance Use Weights - School Disadvantage ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # run regression substance_econhardship <- svyglm( Zsubuse_W3 ~ Zeconhardship, design = design_w3, family = gaussian() ) #save beta and p value dat_w3$substance_econ <- coef(substance_econhardship)[2] substance_econ_B <- coef(substance_econhardship)[2] substance_econ_P <-summary(substance_econhardship)$coefficients["Zeconhardship", "Pr(>|t|)"] ``` ::: Substance Use Weights - Family SES ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # run regression substance_famSES_disadv <- svyglm( Zsubuse_W3 ~ famSES_disadv, design = design_w3, family = gaussian() ) #save beta and p value dat_w3$substance_fam <- coef(substance_famSES_disadv)[2] substance_famSES_B <- coef(substance_famSES_disadv)[2] substance_famSES_P <-summary(substance_famSES_disadv)$coefficients["famSES_disadv", "Pr(>|t|)"] ``` ::: Substance Use Weights - Neighborhood Disadvantage, Subjective ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # run regression substance_nbhd_subj_disadv <- svyglm( Zsubuse_W3 ~ Znbhd_subj_disadv, design = design_w3, family = gaussian() ) #save beta and p value dat_w3$substance_nbhdsub <- coef(substance_nbhd_subj_disadv)[2] substance_nbhdsub_B <- coef(substance_nbhd_subj_disadv)[2] substance_nbhdsub_P <-summary(substance_nbhd_subj_disadv)$coefficients["Znbhd_subj_disadv", "Pr(>|t|)"] ``` ::: Substance Use Weights - Neighborhood Disadvantage, Census ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # run regression education_minorityD <- svyglm( Zedattain_W3 ~ minorityD, design = design_w3, family = gaussian() ) #save beta and p value dat_w3$education_minorityD <- coef(education_minorityD)[2] education_minorityD_B <- coef(education_minorityD)[2] education_minorityD_P <- summary(education_minorityD)$coefficients["minorityD", "Pr(>|t|)"] ``` ::: Education Weights - School Disadvantage ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # ``` ::: ::: Family SES disadvantage is the strongest predictor across all four outcomes (\|*b*\| = 0.13–0.58), and minority status shows the largest effect specifically for substance use (*b* = -0.40) and education (*b* =-0.25). All predictor-outcome associations are significant at *p* \<.001, supporting the use of each as a weighted component of its outcome-specific composite below. ## Structural Disadvantage Composites {#cumulative-adversity-composites} Each outcome's composite is a weighted average of the six structural disadvantage indicators, where the weight for each indicator is the beta extracted above (indicator value × its beta for this specific outcome). This means the same six indicators contribute differently to each of the four composites, based on each indicator's empirical association with that outcome. ::: {.callout-important appearance="minimal" icon="false"} A predictor with a stronger relationship to depression, for example, is weighted more heavily in the depression composite than in the substance use composite. The descriptives of the structural disadvantage composites can be found in @tbl-cumulative. ::: **Compute Composites & Add to Dataset** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # compute weighted composites for all four outcomes dat_w3 <- dat_w3 %>% mutate( # depression composite cumadv_depression = ( (minorityD) * dep_minorityD + (Zschool_disadv) * dep_school + (Zeconhardship) * dep_econ + (famSES_disadv) * dep_fam + (Znbhd_subj_disadv) * dep_nbhdsub + (Zcens_nbhd_disadv) * dep_censnbhd), # substance use composite cumadv_substance = ( (minorityD) * substance_minorityD + (Zschool_disadv) * substance_school + (Zeconhardship) * substance_econ + (famSES_disadv) * substance_fam + (Znbhd_subj_disadv) * substance_nbhdsub + (Zcens_nbhd_disadv) * substance_censnbhd), # education composite cumadv_education = ( (minorityD) * education_minorityD + (Zschool_disadv) * education_school + (Zeconhardship) * education_econ + (famSES_disadv) * education_fam + (Znbhd_subj_disadv) * education_nbhdsub + (Zcens_nbhd_disadv) * education_censnbhd), #health composite cumadv_health = ( (minorityD) * health_minorityD + (Zschool_disadv) * health_school + (Zeconhardship) * health_econ + (famSES_disadv) * health_fam + (Znbhd_subj_disadv) * health_nbhdsub + (Zcens_nbhd_disadv) * health_censnbhd)) # standardize composites and add into dataset dat_w3 <- dat_w3 %>% mutate( Zcumadv_depression = as.numeric(scale(cumadv_depression)), Zcumadv_substance = as.numeric(scale(cumadv_substance)), Zcumadv_education = as.numeric(scale(cumadv_education)), Zcumadv_health = as.numeric(scale(cumadv_health))) # rerun design with composite variables now added to dataset design_w3 <- svydesign( ids = ~1, weights = ~GSWGT3_2, data = dat_w3) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # create table labels for each outcome cumadv_vars <- c( "cumadv_depression" = "Depression", "cumadv_substance" = "Substance Use", "cumadv_education" = "Education Attainment", "cumadv_health" = "General Health") # ``` ::: ::: # Step 1: Cumulative Disadvantage to Outcome {#cumulative-disadvantage} Now, regress each outcome onto its respective (standardized) structural disadvantage composite, the results can be found in @tbl-disadvantage-regressions. **Step 1 Regressions** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Model: Disadvantage → CES-D Depression model_depression <- svyglm( ZcesD_sum ~ Zcumadv_depression, design = design_w3, family = gaussian() ) # Model: Disadvantage → Substance Use model_substance <- svyglm( Zsubuse_W3 ~ Zcumadv_substance, design = design_w3, family = gaussian() ) # Model: Disadvantage → Education Attainment model_education <- svyglm( Zedattain_W3 ~ Zcumadv_education, design = design_w3, family = gaussian() ) # Model: Disadvantage → General Health model_health <- svyglm( Zgenhealth_W3 ~ Zcumadv_health, design = design_w3, family = gaussian() ) ``` ::: **Step 1 Table Creation** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # create function to pull beta and p value from step 1 regressions fmt_step1 <- function(model, var) { coefs <- summary(model)$coefficients b <- coefs[var, "Estimate"] p <- coefs[var, "Pr(>|t|)"] stars <- case_when( p < .001 ~ "***", p < .01 ~ "**", p < .05 ~ "*", p < .10 ~ "^", TRUE ~ "" ) paste0(formatC(b, digits = 2, format = "f"), stars) } # create dataframe for regression table step1_tbl <- data.frame( Predictor = "Cumulative Disadvantage", Depression = fmt_step1(model_depression, "Zcumadv_depression"), Substance_Use = fmt_step1(model_substance, "Zcumadv_substance"), Education = fmt_step1(model_education, "Zcumadv_education"), Health = fmt_step1(model_health, "Zcumadv_health")) # create table for step 1 regressions disadvantage_regressions <- flextable(step1_tbl) |> set_header_labels( Predictor = "", Depression = "Depression", Substance_Use = "Substance Use", Education = "Education", Health = "General Health" ) |> add_header_row( values = c("", "Unstandardized Coefficients (b)"), colwidths = c(1, 4) ) |> theme_apa() |> font(fontname = "Times New Roman", part = "all") |> fontsize(size = 11, part = "all") |> bold(part = "header") |> width(j = 1, width = 2.0) |> width(j = 2:5, width = 1.4) |> align(j = 2:5, align = "center", part = "all") |> add_footer_lines("^ p < .10. * p < .05. ** p < .01. *** p < .001.") |> fontsize(size = 9, part = "footer") |> italic(part = "footer") ``` ::: ::: {#tbl-disadvantage-regressions .cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: Structural disadvantage significantly predicts all four Wave III outcomes (*p* \< .001): higher disadvantage is associated with more depressive symptoms (*b* = 0.15), more substance use (*b* = 0.22), lower educational attainment (*b* = 0.48), and worse general health (*b* = 0.12). These results support the hypothesis higher disadvantage in adolescence is associated with worse outcomes in young adulthood.. The residuals from these models (the gap between predicted and observed outcomes) become the resilience scores used in Step 3. # Step 2: Residuals For each outcome, the residual from its Step 1 model reflects how much better or worse an young adult is doing than their adolescent disadvantage level would predict. A positive residual is "better than expected" (resilient) and a negative residual is "worse than expected" (vulnerable). Depression and substance use residuals are reverse-coded (`* -1`) so that, consistent with education and health, higher values always indicate greater resilience. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # ── Depression ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── dep_int <- coef(model_depression)[1] dep_Zcumadv <- coef(model_depression)[2] dat_w3$predicted_depression <- dep_int + dep_Zcumadv * dat_w3$Zcumadv_depression dat_w3$residual_depression <- dat_w3$ZcesD_sum - dat_w3$predicted_depression # flip: higher = more resilient dat_w3$residual_depressionR <- dat_w3$residual_depression * -1 # ── Substance Use ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── substance_int <- coef(model_substance)[1] substance_Zcumadv <- coef(model_substance)[2] dat_w3$predicted_substance <- substance_int + substance_Zcumadv * dat_w3$Zcumadv_substance dat_w3$residual_substance <- dat_w3$Zsubuse_W3 - dat_w3$predicted_substance # flip: higher = more resilient dat_w3$residual_substanceR <- dat_w3$residual_substance * -1 # ── Education ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── education_int <- coef(model_education)[1] education_Zcumadv <- coef(model_education)[2] dat_w3$predicted_education <- education_int + education_Zcumadv * dat_w3$Zcumadv_education dat_w3$residual_education <- dat_w3$Zedattain_W3 - dat_w3$predicted_education # ── Health ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── health_int <- coef(model_health)[1] health_Zcumadv <- coef(model_health)[2] dat_w3$predicted_health <- health_int + health_Zcumadv * dat_w3$Zcumadv_health dat_w3$residual_health <- dat_w3$Zgenhealth_W3 - dat_w3$predicted_health # rerun design with residual variables added design_w3 <- svydesign( ids = ~1, weights = ~GSWGT3_2, data = dat_w3) ``` ::: # Step 3: Protective Factors Now, regress the residual scores on each (standardized) protective factor, resulting in results for depression (@tbl-step3-depression), substance use (@tbl-step3-substance), education (@tbl-step3-education), and health (@tbl-step3-health). **Residual Regressions** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # ── Depression ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── depression_protect <- svyglm( residual_depressionR ~ Zcommconnect + Zcommintegr_disadv + Zopt_hopeful + Zselfesteem + Zself_efficacy + Zparentchild_rel + Zschoolconnect + bio_sexD + Zwave3age, design = design_w3, family = gaussian() ) # ── Substance Use ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── substance_protect <- svyglm( residual_substanceR ~ Zcommconnect + Zcommintegr_disadv + Zopt_hopeful + Zselfesteem + Zself_efficacy + Zparentchild_rel + Zschoolconnect + bio_sexD + Zwave3age, design = design_w3, family = gaussian() ) # ── Education ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── education_protect <- svyglm( residual_education ~ Zcommconnect + Zcommintegr_disadv + Zopt_hopeful + Zselfesteem + Zself_efficacy + Zparentchild_rel + Zschoolconnect + bio_sexD + Zwave3age, design = design_w3, family = gaussian() ) # ── Health ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── health_protect <- svyglm( residual_health ~ Zcommconnect + Zcommintegr_disadv + Zopt_hopeful + Zselfesteem + Zself_efficacy + Zparentchild_rel + Zschoolconnect + bio_sexD + Zwave3age, design = design_w3, family = gaussian() ) ``` ::: **Create Step 3 Tables** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # create variable labels for protective factors var_labels_step3 <- list( Zcommconnect ~ "Community Connectedness", Zcommintegr_disadv ~ "Community Integration", Zopt_hopeful ~ "Optimism / Hopefulness", Zselfesteem ~ "Self-Esteem", Zself_efficacy ~ "Self-Efficacy", Zparentchild_rel ~ "Parent-Child Relationship", Zschoolconnect ~ "School Connectedness", bio_sexD ~ "Sex (0 = Male)", Zwave3age ~ "Age") # create function for table fmt_tbl_regression <- function(model) { tbl_regression(model, exponentiate = FALSE, label = var_labels_step3) |> bold_p(t = .05) |> bold_labels() |> italicize_levels() |> modify_header(label = "**Variable**") |> modify_footnote(everything() ~ NA) |> as_flex_table() |> flextable::font(fontname = "Times New Roman", part = "all") |> flextable::fontsize(size = 12, part = "all") |> flextable::theme_apa() } # run function for each outcome to generate four tables tbl_step3_depression <- fmt_tbl_regression(depression_protect) tbl_step3_substance <- fmt_tbl_regression(substance_protect) tbl_step3_education <- fmt_tbl_regression(education_protect) tbl_step3_health <- fmt_tbl_regression(health_protect) ``` ::: ::: {#tbl-step3-depression .cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: Self-esteem (β = 0.14, *p* \< .001) and school connectedness (β = 0.11, *p* \< .001) are the only individual- and school-level factors significant for health resilience; the community-level factors (connectedness, integration) are not significant here, unlike their role in the depression and education models. # Step 4: Protective vs. Promotive Comparing the low- and high-disadvantage subsamples distinguishes two types of effects: **promotive** factors are significant regardless of disadvantage level (help everyone similarly), while **protective** factors are significant specifically, or more strongly, in the high-disadvantage subsample (buffer against disadvantages' effects). A factor with a larger, more significant coefficient in the High Disadvantage column than the Low Disadvantage column is acting protectively; one with similar, significant coefficients across both columns is acting promotively. ::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" icon="false"} Results can be found in the following tables: depression (@tbl-compare-depression), substance use (@tbl-compare-substance), education (@tbl-compare-education), and health (@tbl-compare-health). ::: **Split sample into bottom third and top third of structural disadvantage** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # save outcome-specific disadvantage splits as variables in dat_w3 dat_w3$disadvantage_depression <- quantcut(dat_w3$Zcumadv_depression, c(0, .33, .66, 1), lab = c("lo", "mid", "hi")) dat_w3$disadvantage_substance <- quantcut(dat_w3$Zcumadv_substance, c(0, .33, .66, 1), lab = c("lo", "mid", "hi")) dat_w3$disadvantage_education <- quantcut(dat_w3$Zcumadv_education, c(0, .33, .66, 1), lab = c("lo", "mid", "hi")) dat_w3$disadvantage_health <- quantcut(dat_w3$Zcumadv_health, c(0, .33, .66, 1), lab = c("lo", "mid", "hi")) # rerun design with split variables added design_w3 <- svydesign( ids = ~1, weights = ~GSWGT3_2, data = dat_w3) ``` ::: **Run residual regressions with each sub sample, for each outcome.** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # ── Depression ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── model_depression_lo <- svyglm( residual_depressionR ~ Zcommconnect + Zcommintegr_disadv + Zopt_hopeful + Zselfesteem + Zself_efficacy + Zparentchild_rel + Zschoolconnect + bio_sexD + Zwave3age, design = subset(design_w3, disadvantage_depression == "lo"), family = gaussian() ) model_depression_hi <- svyglm( residual_depressionR ~ Zcommconnect + Zcommintegr_disadv + Zopt_hopeful + Zselfesteem + Zself_efficacy + Zparentchild_rel + Zschoolconnect + bio_sexD + Zwave3age, design = subset(design_w3, disadvantage_depression == "hi"), family = gaussian() ) # ── Substance Use ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── model_substance_lo <- svyglm( residual_substanceR ~ Zcommconnect + Zcommintegr_disadv + Zopt_hopeful + Zselfesteem + Zself_efficacy + Zparentchild_rel + Zschoolconnect + bio_sexD + Zwave3age, design = subset(design_w3, disadvantage_substance == "lo"), family = gaussian() ) model_substance_hi <- svyglm( residual_substanceR ~ Zcommconnect + Zcommintegr_disadv + Zopt_hopeful + Zselfesteem + Zself_efficacy + Zparentchild_rel + Zschoolconnect + bio_sexD + Zwave3age, design = subset(design_w3, disadvantage_substance == "hi"), family = gaussian() ) # ── Education ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── model_education_lo <- svyglm( residual_education ~ Zcommconnect + Zcommintegr_disadv + Zopt_hopeful + Zselfesteem + Zself_efficacy + Zparentchild_rel + Zschoolconnect + bio_sexD + Zwave3age, design = subset(design_w3, disadvantage_education == "lo"), family = gaussian() ) model_education_hi <- svyglm( residual_education ~ Zcommconnect + Zcommintegr_disadv + Zopt_hopeful + Zselfesteem + Zself_efficacy + Zparentchild_rel + Zschoolconnect + bio_sexD + Zwave3age, design = subset(design_w3, disadvantage_education == "hi"), family = gaussian() ) # ── Health ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── model_health_lo <- svyglm( residual_health ~ Zcommconnect + Zcommintegr_disadv + Zopt_hopeful + Zselfesteem + Zself_efficacy + Zparentchild_rel + Zschoolconnect + bio_sexD + Zwave3age, design = subset(design_w3, disadvantage_health == "lo"), family = gaussian() ) model_health_hi <- svyglm( residual_health ~ Zcommconnect + Zcommintegr_disadv + Zopt_hopeful + Zselfesteem + Zself_efficacy + Zparentchild_rel + Zschoolconnect + bio_sexD + Zwave3age, design = subset(design_w3, disadvantage_health == "hi"), family = gaussian() ) ``` ::: **Create Step 4 Tables** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # create function to make comparison table make_protect_table <- function(model_full, model_lo, model_hi, outcome_label) { protective_vars <- c( "Zcommconnect", "Zcommintegr_disadv", "Zopt_hopeful", "Zselfesteem", "Zself_efficacy", "Zparentchild_rel", "Zschoolconnect" ) var_labels <- c( "Zcommconnect" = "Community Connectedness", "Zcommintegr_disadv" = "Community Integration", "Zopt_hopeful" = "Optimism / Hopefulness", "Zselfesteem" = "Self-Esteem", "Zself_efficacy" = "Self-Efficacy", "Zparentchild_rel" = "Parent-Child Relationship", "Zschoolconnect" = "School Connectedness" ) fmt_coef <- function(model, var) { coefs <- summary(model)$coefficients if (!var %in% rownames(coefs)) return("—") b <- coefs[var, "Estimate"] p <- coefs[var, "Pr(>|t|)"] stars <- case_when( p < .001 ~ "***", p < .01 ~ "**", p < .05 ~ "*", p < .10 ~ "^", TRUE ~ "" ) paste0(formatC(b, digits = 2, format = "f"), stars) } tbl <- data.frame( Variable = var_labels[protective_vars], Full_Sample = sapply(protective_vars, \(v) fmt_coef(model_full, v)), Low_Disadvantage = sapply(protective_vars, \(v) fmt_coef(model_lo, v)), High_Disadvantage = sapply(protective_vars, \(v) fmt_coef(model_hi, v)), row.names = NULL ) flextable(tbl) |> set_header_labels( Variable = "Protective Factor", Full_Sample = "Full Sample", Low_Disadvantage = "Low Disadvantage", High_Disadvantage = "High Disadvantage" ) |> add_header_row( values = c("", outcome_label), colwidths = c(1, 3) ) |> theme_apa() |> font(fontname = "Times New Roman", part = "all") |> fontsize(size = 11, part = "all") |> bold(part = "header") |> width(j = 1, width = 2.2) |> width(j = 2:4, width = 1.5) |> align(j = 2:4, align = "center", part = "all") |> add_footer_lines("^ p < .10. * p < .05. ** p < .01. *** p < .001.") |> fontsize(size = 9, part = "footer") |> italic(part = "footer") } # run function for each outcome tbl_compare_depression <- make_protect_table( depression_protect, model_depression_lo, model_depression_hi, "Depression") tbl_compare_substance <- make_protect_table( substance_protect, model_substance_lo, model_substance_hi, "Substance Use") tbl_compare_education <- make_protect_table( education_protect, model_education_lo, model_education_hi, "Education Attainment") tbl_compare_health <- make_protect_table( health_protect, model_health_lo, model_health_hi, "General Health") ``` ::: ::: {#tbl-compare-depression .cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
